subject: feminism
title: Care ethics: Gilligan's challenge to Kohlberg's justice-only model, then Noddings, Tronto, and the politics of dependency
dek: How the ethics of care emerged as a critique of moral psychology's justice-and-rights paradigm, what it claims about interdependence and responsibility for concrete others, who developed it philosophically and politically from the 1980s onward, and how it named unpaid care labor as moral and political fact.
era: Gilligan's In a Different Voice 1982; Noddings's Caring 1984; Tronto's Moral Boundaries 1993; ongoing debates on care as public good

honesty: This lesson treats care ethics as a named philosophical tradition following Gilligan 1982, Noddings 1984, Tronto 1993.

timeline.label: In a Different Voice
timeline.detail: Carol Gilligan published In a Different Voice (Harvard University Press). Critiqued Kohlberg's stages, proposed care as a moral orientation.

timeline.label: Noddings: Caring
timeline.detail: Nel Noddings published Caring. Developed care ethics for education.

timeline.label: Tronto: Moral Boundaries
timeline.detail: Joan C. Tronto published Moral Boundaries. Moved care ethics to political economy.

read.title: Carol Gilligan — In a Different Voice (1982)

glossary.explain: Moral approach emphasizing interdependence, attentiveness, responsibility for concrete others, and relationships.
American psychologist born 1936. Published In a Different Voice in 1982, naming care ethics.

blocks.text: Care ethics argues that moral life is about interdependence, attentiveness to need, responsibility for concrete others, and maintaining relationships. Not deficient versions of justice reasoning; a distinct moral orientation.
When you make a moral judgment, do you ask only about justice and rules, or do you also ask: who will do the care work, whose needs are attended to, what relationships are sustained or broken?
